Receipt lines for a batch. Send batch_num (required, 1 or more) and batch_date. A missing batch_date is not rejected; it simply matches nothing. receivedate is the time of your request, not the time the stock was received. expirydate is YYYY-MM-DD. No data is a 200 with a plain string: "Unable to find data for given request.". Existing integrations. POST /api/v1/inbound/orders Tell us what inbound stock to expect (an ASN): PO number, expected delivery date, and SKUs with quantities, plus the lot number where your items are lot-tracked. One element per line. Each element of orders is one PO line: clientcode, ponumber, deliverydate, sku and quantity are required. Send JSON. A Content-Type other than application/json is answered 415. Validation accumulates: a 400 lists every problem it found for a line, not just the first. quantity must be a whole number above 0. deliverydate must be a real date (US Eastern). unitofmeasure, source, externalOrderId and rmaId are accepted for compatibility but not used. Existing integrations. POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel Cancel an order by its pick ticket ID. This works only before the order has shipping or tracking information and while it is still open; otherwise the response says the order could not be cancelled. Cancel by your pick ticket. The response is 200 whenever the request is valid; read order_cancelled to see whether it worked. Orders are created in the background, usually within seconds of a successful submit. Until then, cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled: wait a few seconds and try again. Only open orders with no shipping or tracking information can be cancelled. Assembly orders cannot be cancelled through the API, and cancel finds only orders placed under your own owner code (not a related account's). If the order had already been released to the warehouse, a successful cancel marks it "do not ship" in Capacity, but contact Capacity Support straight away so the warehouse can stop it. Keep pick tickets unique. If two open orders share one, which order is cancelled is not defined. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/cancel, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 500 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Internal Server Error

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders Send one or more outbound orders for fulfilment. Each valid order in the request is accepted even if others fail; a 400 response names one order that failed and why (not every failure), so fix the orders that failed and resend only those. Values are strings and names are lowercase. Quantities, amounts and flags are all strings ("2", not 2). Quantities are whole numbers, digits only. Required per order: the fields marked required, plus shipname or shipbusinessname (at least one), and at least one line. An order with an empty lines array is skipped. Always send lines: an order sent without the field is accepted with no lines. Defaults: an empty or omitted retailercode becomes WEB, and empty or omitted single-character flags become N. A flag that is only spaces is rejected. itemproductid, buyeritemnumber and itemproductdesc longer than 50 characters are cut to 50 rather than rejected. Partial acceptance: when individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason (not every failure). Fix and resend only the orders that failed. Nothing is accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail (a null order or line, or no order with lines). 500 or 504 with {"accepted": false}: some orders may not have been accepted. Resending the same request within 24 hours is generally safe: orders already accepted with identical content are recognised and skipped. Some accounts receive 504 instead of 500; treat them the same. Do not retry automatically after a timeout with no response. The orders may have been accepted in full, and this API does not return order IDs you could check. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent. Dates (orderdate, requestedshipdate, canceldate, requesteddeliverydate, deliverybydate) are read as US Eastern dates. Use YYYY-MM-DD. A requestedshipdate more than 3 days out normally holds the order as a future order until nearer the date. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/create, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 500 504 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Internal Server Error Gateway Timeout

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/status Your picked orders (status: picked, awaiting shipment) with their lines, cartons and tracking. Every order of yours that is currently picked is returned, plus the Capacity order IDs you send if they have been picked; orders belonging to related accounts (same parent client) are included. A requested ID that has not been picked, or does not exist, comes back as a "not found" entry; if nothing is found the response is 404. This returns picked orders. An order appears once it has been picked (and until it ships). Every order of yours that is currently picked is returned, even ones you did not ask for, plus the orders you ask for by Capacity order number (orderIds) if they have been picked. Orders belonging to your related accounts (same parent client) are included. An order that exists but has not been picked yet comes back as a "not found" entry. If nothing at all is found, the response is 404. Use shipment confirmations, not this call, to learn what has shipped. orderIds are Capacity order numbers (as returned in capacityOrderNum by carrier tracking events), not your pick tickets. orderStatusDate and pickedOrderStatusDate are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm; releaseDate and currentSLADate are MM/DD/YYYY; all US Eastern with no offset. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/status/picked, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 404 500 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Not Found Internal Server Error

POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/shipments Ship confirmations for your orders for the batch number and batch date you send (both required): what shipped, order totals, carrier, service and tracking numbers. Polling, not callbacks. Capacity prepares ship confirmations in numbered batches each day (batch_num 1, 2, 3 ...). Your onboarding contact tells you how many batches your account receives per day. Request each batch for a batch_date after it has been prepared, and match lines to your orders by pickticketid. Batch 1 starts the evening before. Batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. One item per order line. shipDate is ISO 8601 without an offset (US Eastern). expiryDate is MM/DD/YYYY, or empty when there is none. No data is a 200. When a batch has no confirmations, the response is 200 {"message": "No records found. Please check input."}, not an empty list. Check the body before reading it as data. Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /api/order/track, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 401 500 OK Bad Request Unauthorized Internal Server Error

Poll by hour. hour_num is the hour of day, 0-23, in US Eastern time (0 is midnight to 00:59). batch_date is the Eastern calendar date. POST /api/v1/auth/token Exchange your client ID and secret for a bearer token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every other call. Tokens last about 15 minutes; expires_in in the response gives the exact number of seconds. Form post, not JSON. Send grant_type=client_credentials with your client_id and client_secret, either as form fields or as an HTTP Basic Authorization header (client_id:client_secret, base64). If both are present, the header is used. Secrets are case-sensitive. Reuse the token. It lasts about 15 minutes (expires_in, in seconds). Cache it and request a new one shortly before it expires; do not request a token per call. Errors use the OAuth shape, not {"message": ...}: 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": ...}, 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"}, and 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", "error_description": ...} when the token service is briefly unavailable (retry with backoff). Existing integrations. Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API may keep calling POST /Token, at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com, with the same request and response. New integrations must use this path; a new integration calling the previous path gets 410.
Responses​ 200 400 503 OK Bad Request Service Unavailable
The Partner API uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow. Your integration exchanges a client ID and secret for a short-lived access token, then sends that token on every request.

Credential Format Notes Client ID Text, issued by Capacity Not secret, but do not publish it. Client secret Text, issued by Capacity Secret and case-sensitive. Sandbox and production credentials are issued separately. See Environments.

POST /api/v1/auth/token with a form body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): Field Value grant_type client_credentials (the only grant supported) client_id Your client ID client_secret Your client secret You can send the ID and secret as an HTTP Basic Authorization header instead of form fields. If you send both, the header is used. cURL # Form fields curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "client_id=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" # Or HTTP Basic curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -u "$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID:$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -d "grant_type=client_credentials" The response: Field Meaning access_token The token. Treat it as an opaque string: do not parse it or rely on its contents. token_type Always bearer. expires_in Seconds until the token expires (about 900). .issued, .expires When the token was issued and expires, as RFC 1123 dates in GMT.
Send it on every request except the token request: Request header Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.EXAMPLE-ONLY.signature

Request a token once and reuse it until about 60 seconds before it expires. Requesting a token for every call is slower for you and may be limited in future. Node.js Python C# let cached = { token: null, expiresAt: 0 }; async function getToken() { if (cached.token && Date.now() < cached.expiresAt - 60_000) { return cached.token; } const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }, body: new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "client_credentials", client_id: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID, client_secret: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET, }), }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Token request failed: ${response.status}`); const body = await response.json(); cached = { token: body.access_token, expiresAt: Date.now() + body.expires_in * 1000 }; return cached.token; } import os, time, requests _cached = {"token": None, "expires_at": 0.0} def get_token() -> str: if _cached["token"] and time.time() < _cached["expires_at"] - 60: return _cached["token"] response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", data={ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID"], "client_secret": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET"], }, timeout=30, ) response.raise_for_status() body = response.json() _cached.update(token=body["access_token"], expires_at=time.time() + body["expires_in"]) return _cached["token"] public sealed class CapacityTokenProvider(HttpClient http, string clientId, string clientSecret) { private readonly SemaphoreSlim gate = new(1, 1); private string? token; private DateTimeOffset expiresAt; public async Task<string> GetTokenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { await gate.WaitAsync(cancellationToken); try { if (token is not null && DateTimeOffset.UtcNow < expiresAt.AddSeconds(-60)) { return token; } using var response = await http.PostAsync("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = clientId, ["client_secret"] = clientSecret, }), cancellationToken); response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken)); token = json.RootElement.GetProperty("access_token").GetString()!; expiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddSeconds(json.RootElement.GetProperty("expires_in").GetInt32()); return token; } finally { gate.Release(); } } } On a 401 If a call returns 401, the token may have expired early or been revoked. Get a new token and retry the call once. If it fails again, stop and check your credentials.

Response Cause Fix 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", ...} Wrong or missing client ID or secret, or the credentials are disabled. Check both values and the case of the secret. Check you are not using sandbox credentials in production. 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"} grant_type is missing or not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", ...} The token service is briefly unavailable. Retry after a few seconds, with backoff. 401 on any other call Missing, malformed or expired token. Get a new token and retry once.

Never expose the client secret Anyone with the secret can submit and cancel orders as you. Store the secret in a secrets manager or an environment variable. Never commit it or write it to logs. Call the API from your servers only. Never put the secret in a browser, mobile app or anything a customer can download. Do not share one credential between unrelated systems; ask for a separate one. If a secret may have been exposed, contact Capacity Support straight away so it can be replaced.

Integrations built for the previous Capacity REST API, at api-integration.capacityllc.com, may keep calling POST /Token with their existing credentials. It behaves the same as POST /api/v1/auth/token. New integrations must use POST /api/v1/auth/token at api-partner.capacityllc.com. See Existing integrations.
Changes to the Partner API that an integration can notice, newest first. Read Versioning and changes for what can change within v1.

Partner API documentation published. The v1 reference covers 12 operations. They are the access token and connection test; outbound orders (submit, cancel, picked orders); shipment confirmations (by order line and by carton) and carrier tracking events; receiving orders and receipt confirmations; and inventory (by SKU, and by lot and LPN). The OpenAPI document and a Postman collection are available to download.
Email itedi@capacityllc.com. Ask for sandbox credentials to build and test, and for production credentials when you are ready to go live. See Environments.
No. A successful submit returns {"accepted": true}. Refer to an order by your pick ticket (pickticketid), which must be unique per order.
documents.s: Does submitting an order return an order ID?

documents.t: Poll shipment confirmations by batch. The Partner API has no webhooks or callbacks. See Send orders and track shipments.
documents.s: How do I know an order has shipped?

documents.t: Batch 1 starts at 22:00 the evening before Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. See Dates and time zones.
documents.s: Why is my order missing from batch 1?

documents.t: Do not resend orders automatically after a timeout If a Submit orders request times out with no response, the orders may have been accepted in full, and the API returns no order IDs you could check. Resending can create duplicate orders. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.
documents.s: My request timed out. Should I resend the orders?

documents.t: About 15 minutes (expires_in, in seconds). Reuse it, and get a new one shortly before it expires.
documents.s: How long does an access token last?

documents.t: Not enforced today; follow the fair-use guidelines.

No. Existing integrations keep working at api-integration.capacityllc.com with the same paths, requests and responses. To move to the current paths, follow Previous REST API paths. New integrations must use api-partner.capacityllc.com and the /api/v1/ paths.
documents.s: We already use the previous Capacity REST API. Do we need to change anything?

documents.t: Yes: import the Postman collection, or use the OpenAPI document in your API tool of choice.
documents.s: Can I try requests without writing code?

documents.t: The Partner API has two environments. They have different base URLs, different credentials and different data. Nothing you do in one affects the other. Sandbox Production Base URL https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com https://api-partner.capacityllc.com Credentials Sandbox client ID and secret Production client ID and secret Data Test data. Orders are not fulfilled or shipped to real customers. Live. Orders are picked, packed and shipped. Use it for Building and testing your integration Your live integration, after go-live Use the Sandbox | Production switch at the top of every page to change the base URL in all code samples. The coloured band under the navigation bar shows which one is selected. New integrations use api-partner New integrations must use api-partner.capacityllc.com. Capacity does not support new integrations at any other address.

Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API call https://api-integration.capacityllc.com. That address is moving to this same API, so existing integrations keep working without changes: The previous paths (for example POST /api/order/create and POST /Token) keep working for existing integrations at both api-integration.capacityllc.com and api-partner.capacityllc.com. The request and response formats do not change. api-integration.capacityllc.com is for existing integrations only. It is not offered to new clients. Capacity will ask existing integrations to move to api-partner.capacityllc.com and the /api/v1/ paths. See Paths and versions and the legacy path map in the API reference.

Keep the base URL in configuration. Your code should read one setting for the base URL and one for each credential. Going live, or moving from api-integration to api-partner, is then a configuration change, not a code change. Never mix the pairs. A sandbox token is rejected by production and a production token is rejected by the sandbox. A configuration that points production credentials at the sandbox URL fails in a way that is easy to misread as "wrong password". Label your logs. Log which environment each request went to, and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.

Every current path starts with /api/v1/. Paths without /v1/ (for example /api/order/create) belong to the previous Capacity REST API and are kept only for integrations built against it. A new integration that calls one gets 410 Gone with the current path in the message. See the API reference, where those paths are marked deprecated.

Email itedi@capacityllc.com to request Partner API sandbox credentials. You receive: Item Example in these docs What it is Client ID YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID Identifies your integration. Client secret YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET A password for your integration. Case-sensitive. Owner code ZZ The 2-character code for your account. You send it as clientcode on orders and client on inventory requests. Ship method and retailer codes GROUND, WEB The codes agreed for your account during onboarding. Sandbox and production credentials are different. Sandbox credentials do not work in production, and production credentials do not work in the sandbox. Keep the secret out of code Load the client secret from an environment variable or a secrets manager. Never commit it, put it in a URL, or send it from a browser. The samples read the credentials from environment variables: Set your sandbox credentials export CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID="YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID" export CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET="YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET"

Exchange the client ID and secret for a bearer token. The request is a form post, not JSON. cURL Node.js Python C# POST /api/v1/auth/token curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "client_id=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" POST /api/v1/auth/token const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "client_credentials", client_id: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID, client_secret: process.env.CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET, }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); POST /api/v1/auth/token import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", headers={ "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, data={ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID"], "client_secret": os.environ["CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET"], }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) POST /api/v1/auth/token using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token"); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID")!, ["client_secret"] = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET")!, }); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.EXAMPLE-ONLY.signature", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 899, ".issued": "Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:00:00 GMT", ".expires": "Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:14:59 GMT" } Keep the access_token for the next steps: Keep the token export CAPACITY_TOKEN="paste the access_token here" Reuse the token The token lasts about 15 minutes. Reuse it until shortly before expires_in runs out; do not request a new token for every call. See Authentication for token caching. If you get It means Do this 400 invalid_credentials The client ID or secret is wrong, or the credentials are disabled. Check both values, including the case of the secret. Check you are using sandbox credentials against the sandbox. 400 unsupported_grant_type grant_type is not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 temporarily_unavailable The token service is briefly unavailable. Wait a few seconds and retry.

cURL Node.js Python C# GET /api/v1/ping curl "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" GET /api/v1/ping const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping", { method: "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); GET /api/v1/ping import os import uuid import requests response = requests.get( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) GET /api/v1/ping using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/ping"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 "Connection is successful." A 401 with {"message": "Authorization has been denied for this request."} means the header is missing, malformed (it must be Bearer, a space, then the token) or the token has expired. Get a new token and try again.

Send one order with one line. Replace the owner, retailer and ship method codes with yours, and use a SKU that exists for your account. The ship date is a week out, so the order waits as a future order and you can cancel it in the next step. cURL Node.js Python C# POST /api/v1/outbound/orders curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" \ -d '{ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] }' POST /api/v1/outbound/orders const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: JSON.stringify({ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); POST /api/v1/outbound/orders import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, json={ "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1", }, ], }, ], }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) POST /api/v1/outbound/orders using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new StringContent(""" { "orders": [ { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "clientcode": "ZZ", "retailercode": "WEB", "shipname": "Jordan Example", "shipaddress1": "100 Example Street", "shipcity": "Edison", "shipstate": "NJ", "shipzip": "08817", "shipcountry": "US", "shipresidentialflag": "Y", "shipmethod": "GROUND", "requestedshipdate": "2026-11-09", "lines": [ { "itemlinenumber": "1", "itemproductid": "SKU-EXAMPLE-1", "itemorderquantity": "1" } ] } ] } """, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "accepted": true } Strings and lowercase Every value in an order is a string, including quantities ("1", not 1). Field names are lowercase. If an order fails validation you get a 400 that names the field and the pick ticket: 400 Bad Request { "message": "Please validate order data. Shipping Address 1 can not be empty for Pick Ticket Id PT-0001001" } A 400 can mean some orders were accepted When individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason, not every failure. Resend only the orders that failed: check each against the field rules to find them all. Nothing was accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail. The full field list and every response are in Submit orders.

note Orders are created in the background, usually within seconds. If cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled, wait a few seconds and try again. cURL Node.js Python C# POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPACITY_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Correlation-ID: $(uuidgen)" \ -d '{ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" }' POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel const response = await fetch("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CAPACITY_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Correlation-ID": crypto.randomUUID(), }, body: JSON.stringify({ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" }), }); console.log(response.status, await response.json()); POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel import os import uuid import requests response = requests.post( "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CAPACITY_TOKEN']}", "X-Correlation-ID": str(uuid.uuid4()), }, json={ "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", }, timeout=60, ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel using var http = new HttpClient(); using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel"); request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CAPACITY_TOKEN")!); request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-ID", Guid.NewGuid().ToString()); request.Content = new StringContent(""" { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001" } """, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); using var response = await http.SendAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"{(int)response.StatusCode} {await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()}"); Expected response · 200 { "pickticketid": "PT-0001001", "order_cancelled": true, "order_cancelled_result": "Order cancelled successfully." } What "cancelled" means Cancel only works while the order is open and has no shipping or tracking information. Pick tickets should be unique: if two open orders share one, which order is cancelled is not defined.

Before you switch to production: Request production credentials. They are separate from your sandbox credentials. Change the base URL to the production URL. Keep it in configuration, not in code. Store the secret in a secrets manager, not in source control or logs. Reuse one token until shortly before it expires. Treat every date and time from the API as US Eastern time. See Dates and time zones. Retry 500, 503 and 504 with backoff, and send an X-Correlation-ID on every request so support can find it. See Errors.

Two calls report stock. Both take your 2-character owner code as client, matched exactly, including case. Call Use it for Get inventory Quantities per SKU: what you sell against. Get inventory by lot and LPN The same stock broken down by lot, expiry date and LPN (licence plate), with held quantity by reason code.

Nothing to report is null. In Get inventory, inventory is null rather than an empty list. Spelling and types. The field commited is spelled that way; price is a string. No expiry shows as 0001-01-01T00:00:00 in Get inventory by lot and LPN.
Stock changes as orders ship and receipts are put away. A few reads a day, and one an hour at most, keeps you in step; see Fair use.

This guide puts the outbound calls in the order an integration uses them. Each step links to its reference page for every field. Solid arrows are the order's progress in Capacity; dotted arrows are the calls you make to read it.

Submit orders (POST /api/v1/outbound/orders) takes one or more orders, each with its lines. You identify each order by your pick ticket (pickticketid); keep it unique per order. A 200 {"accepted": true} means the orders passed validation and are being created in the background, usually within seconds. Always send each order's lines: an order with an empty lines array is skipped without an error. The response carries no Capacity order IDs. Your pick ticket is how you refer to the order afterwards (cancel, ship confirmations). A requestedshipdate more than 3 days out normally holds the order as a future order until nearer the date. A 400 can mean some orders were accepted When individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason, not every failure. Resend only the orders that failed: check each against the field rules to find them all. Nothing was accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail. Do not resend orders automatically after a timeout If a Submit orders request times out with no response, the orders may have been accepted in full, and the API returns no order IDs you could check. Resending can create duplicate orders. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent. More on retries: Retrying order submissions.

Cancel an order (POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel) cancels by pick ticket. Read order_cancelled in the 200 response: only open orders with no shipping or tracking information can be cancelled. If you cancel in the first seconds after submitting, the order may not exist yet; wait a few seconds and retry.

There are no callbacks: you poll. Capacity prepares ship confirmations in numbered batches per day. Your onboarding contact tells you how many batches your account receives per day, and when each is prepared. For each batch_date (US Eastern), request each batch_num after it has been prepared, with Get shipment confirmations (one item per order line) or Get shipment confirmations by carton (tracking number, SSCC and contents per carton). Match confirmations to your orders by pickticketid, and make processing idempotent: reading the same batch twice must not ship-confirm an order twice in your system. A batch with nothing in it is a 200 with {"message": "No records found. Please check input."}, not an empty list. A batch that has not been prepared yet looks the same, so do not treat an early empty answer as final. Batch 1 starts at 22:00 the evening before Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. See the batch windows drawn out in Dates and time zones.
Get carrier tracking events returns carrier scans for one hour (hour_num 0-23, US Eastern) of a batch_date. Request an hour after it has ended. Events identify the order by capacityOrderNum.

Get picked orders returns orders that have been picked and not yet shipped. It is not a general order-status lookup: an order that has not been picked comes back as "not found", and shipped orders are reported by step 3.

Submit receiving orders (POST /api/v1/inbound/orders) tells the fulfillment center what to expect. Send one element per PO line: clientcode, ponumber, deliverydate, sku and quantity are required on each. quantity is a whole number above 0. deliverydate is a US Eastern date. A 400 lists every problem found for a line, so you can fix them in one pass.

Get receipt confirmations works in batches, like ship confirmations: send batch_num (1 or more) and batch_date. receivedate is not the receipt time receivedate in the response is the time of your request, not the time the stock was received. Always send batch_date. A request without it is not rejected; it matches nothing. When there is nothing to report, the response is 200 with the plain string "Unable to find data for given request.".

What this means for you Ship-confirmation batches Formats Dates and times are US Eastern, with no offset Capacity operates on US Eastern time (America/New_York, EST/EDT). Every order, shipment, inventory and receiving date the Partner API accepts or returns is Eastern wall-clock time, and no time-zone offset is included. Convert explicitly; do not assume UTC. The one exception is the token's .issued and .expires, which are GMT.

Batch dates (batch_date) are Eastern calendar dates; see Ship-confirmation batches for the batch-1 window. Hours (hour_num on tracking events) are Eastern hours, 0–23. 0 is midnight to 00:59 Eastern. Dates you send on orders (orderdate, requestedshipdate, and so on) are read as Eastern dates. Daylight saving time applies. Eastern is UTC−5 in winter and UTC−4 in summer.

Batch 1 starts at 22:00 the evening before Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. Each bar below is the window of confirmation creation times (US Eastern) that a batch of that date covers:

The API keeps the formats of the previous Capacity REST API, so they differ by field: Where Example Format Shipment shipDate; lot expiryDate (inventory by lot and LPN) 2026-11-02T00:00:00 ISO 8601, no offset. A lot with no expiry shows 0001-01-01T00:00:00. Shipment and carton expiryDate; picked-order releaseDate, currentSLADate 11/02/2026 MM/DD/YYYY; empty when not set Picked-order orderStatusDate, pickedOrderStatusDate 2026-11-02 14:05:09.123 YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm Receipt expirydate 2026-11-02 YYYY-MM-DD Receipt receivedate 2026-11-02 YYYY-MM-DD; the time of your request, not of the receipt Token .issued, .expires Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:00:00 GMT RFC 1123, GMT When you send dates, use YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601 (2026-11-02T15:30:00) without an offset.
Error format Status codes No data is not an error Retrying order submissions Backoff Correlation IDs

Most errors from data endpoints are a JSON object with a message: { "message": "Please validate order data. Shipping Address 1 can not be empty for Pick Ticket Id PT-0001001" } Two exceptions: the token endpoint uses the OAuth error shape, and a failed order save on Submit orders returns {"accepted": false} (see Retrying order submissions). The token endpoint's error shape { "error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": "A valid client_Id and client_Secret must be provided." } Match on the status code Read the HTTP status first, then the message. Messages are written for people; match on the status code in your code, not on message text.

Status Meaning Retry? What to do 200 Success. — Some read endpoints also return 200 when nothing matched; see No data is not an error. 400 The request is invalid: malformed JSON, a missing or invalid field, or your account could not be validated. No Fix the request. Validation messages name the field and the pick ticket. 401 Missing, malformed or expired token. Once, with a new token Get a new token and retry once. If it fails again, check your credentials. 404 None of the orders you asked for has been picked, and none is currently picked (Get picked orders). No Check the IDs; use shipment confirmations for shipped orders. 410 You called a path kept only for older integrations. No Use the current /api/v1/ path named in the message. 415 The Content-Type is not JSON. Returned only by Submit orders, Submit receiving orders, Get receipt confirmations, Get inventory and Get inventory by lot and LPN. No Send Content-Type: application/json (text/json is also accepted). 500 Something failed on our side. Yes, with backoff Retry. For order submission, see Retrying order submissions. 503 A service we depend on is briefly unavailable. Yes, with backoff Retry after a few seconds. 504 Returned instead of 500 for some accounts when orders could not be saved. Yes, with backoff Treat exactly like 500. The Partner API does not currently return 403, 409 or 429. Handle any other 4xx as "do not retry" and any other 5xx as "retry with backoff", so your integration keeps working if new codes are introduced.

When nothing matches, some read endpoints answer 200 with a message instead of an empty list: { "message": "No records found. Please check input." } Check the shape of a 200 body before you read it as data.
documents.s: No data is not an error

documents.t: Order submission is the one call where a retry could create duplicates, so it is handled specially. After a 400: A 400 can mean some orders were accepted When individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason, not every failure. Resend only the orders that failed: check each against the field rules to find them all. Nothing was accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail. After a 500 or 504 with {"accepted": false}: some orders may have been accepted. Resending the same request within 24 hours is generally safe: orders already accepted with identical content are recognised and skipped. After a timeout with no response at all: Do not resend orders automatically after a timeout If a Submit orders request times out with no response, the orders may have been accepted in full, and the API returns no order IDs you could check. Resending can create duplicate orders. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.
Wait 2 seconds before the first retry, then double the wait each time (2, 4, 8, 16 seconds), adding up to a second of random jitter. Stop after five attempts and alert someone.

Send an X-Correlation-ID header with a unique value (a UUID) on every request. It is returned on the response. Log it with the request, and when you contact support quote it together with the time of the request and, for orders, the pick tickets.

The Partner API does not enforce request rate limits today. It serves every Capacity client from shared systems, so please follow these guidelines. If an integration's traffic affects other clients, Capacity will contact you. Call Recommended Get an access token Once per token lifetime (about 15 minutes). Cache the token; never request one per call. Submit orders As orders arrive, or grouped into one request every few minutes. Get shipment confirmations (both forms) Each batch after it has been prepared, not repeatedly through the day. Get carrier tracking events Each hour after it has ended, not repeatedly within the hour. Get inventory (both forms) A few times a day; once an hour at most. Get picked orders Once an hour at most. Test the connection For monitoring, once every 5 minutes at most.

Run scheduled jobs at a random minute, not exactly on the hour, so all integrations do not call at once. After an error, back off as described in Errors; never retry in a tight loop. Request the batches and hours you need, rather than re-reading a whole day.
If request limits are introduced, Capacity will announce them in the changelog. Handle any status code you do not recognise as described in Errors.

Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API keep working. They can call these paths with the same requests and responses at api-integration.capacityllc.com or api-partner.capacityllc.com. New integrations must use the /api/v1/ paths; a new integration that calls a previous path gets 410 Gone with the current path in the message. Change the base URL to https://api-partner.capacityllc.com and the token path to /api/v1/auth/token. Your credentials do not change. Change each path using the table above. Request and response bodies are the same, except for the two paths with no direct equivalent. Keep sending the key body field (and apiversion, if you send it today) until Capacity confirms your credentials are set up as a current integration; current integrations send neither. Test in the sandbox before switching production.

partner-api.v1.json is the complete v1 contract (OpenAPI 3). It is generated from the API itself, so it always matches the API reference. Use it to generate a client, to import into an API tool such as Postman, Insomnia or Bruno, or to see what changed between versions.

The collection holds the requests used throughout these docs, with a script that gets and reuses an access token for you. Download the collection and the Sandbox environment (Production environment). In Postman, choose Import and select both files. Select the Sandbox environment. Fill in clientId and clientSecret with your sandbox credentials. Keep the secret in the current value only, so it is never synced or shared. Send Test the connection. The token is fetched automatically. The example values (owner code ZZ, SKU-EXAMPLE-1, the pick ticket and the dates) are placeholders. Replace them with your account's values, and set dates to the future, before sending orders.
The version is in the path: every current operation is under /api/v1/.

These changes are not breaking. They can be made to v1 at any time and are listed in the changelog. Build your integration so that they do not break it: New operations. New optional request fields. New response fields. Ignore fields you do not recognise. New status codes. Handle an unknown 4xx as "do not retry" and an unknown 5xx as "retry with backoff". Changed message text. Match on the status code, never on the message.
documents.s: Changes that can happen within v1

documents.t: These are breaking: removing or renaming a field or operation, making an optional field required, changing a field's type or format, or tightening a limit such as a maximum length. Capacity checks every change to the API's contract for breaking changes before it is released. A breaking change to v1 is listed in the changelog.

The paths of the previous Capacity REST API are kept for existing integrations and marked deprecated in the OpenAPI document. New integrations must use the /api/v1/ paths; see Previous REST API paths.
The complete v1 contract is published at /openapi/partner-api.v1.json. It changes whenever the API reference on this site changes, so you can generate a client from it or compare versions.

Email the Capacity integrations team at itedi@capacityllc.com for: sandbox or production credentials replacing a credential that may have been exposed help with a failing request questions about the API if you are evaluating Capacity Existing clients with a production problem: email itsupport@capacityllc.com to open a support ticket, or contact your Capacity account manager.

Help us find your request quickly: The environment (sandbox or production) The method and path, for example POST /api/v1/outbound/orders The X-Correlation-ID you sent, and the time of the request (with time zone) The HTTP status and the response body Never include your client secret or an access token in a ticket or email.
